answers: Review round 4: two correctness findings in the Go check and three small fixes, each answered on its thread and resolved
head: 9862c8d8b99962284b5fc00075c5a7b41daed9f7

proof.criterion: Review round 4, finding 1 (mirror-ci-images.sh:117): the Go check read a third-party registry on every ci-images run, held rows included, which put a Docker Hub fetch back into a CI job and made .github/ci-images.yaml:10-11 false
proof.surface: The copy script's own harness, whose stand-in crane records every reference it is asked for and reaches no network
proof.observed: 45 assertions, 32 before. The loop now asks the package first: a held row's Go is read at ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion/ci@<the row's digest>, the package's own copy, which crane copy landed at the row's digest, and a row being copied is read at <upstream>@<digest> before the copy, so bytes whose label is wrong never land. Every library/golang row is still checked, held or copied; only the reference changes. The new case 'a run whose package holds every row' asserts that no reference the stand-in was asked for is a docker.io one and none is outside the package.
proof.negativeControl: That case run against the script as the reviewer read it (the parent commit's file put in place, then restored): 'FAIL: reads the Go of the package's own copy', 'FAIL: asks crane for no docker.io reference', 'FAIL: and for no reference outside the package at all'. All six assertions pass at this head.

proof.criterion: Review round 4, finding 2 (mirror-ci-images.sh:88): the copy script decided which rows are Go rows with a parser of its own, which disagreed with check-ci-images.sh's upstream_parts, so a row rules 3 and 7 count as the Go row could escape the Go check
proof.surface: Both harnesses, over fixtures, and the gate over the real tree
proof.observed: One parser: split_reference, upstream_parts, the four grammar regexes and DOCKER_HUB_HOSTS moved out of check-ci-images.sh's heredoc into .github/scripts/ci_images.py, beside workflow_paths.py and imported the same way (PYTHONPATH=.github/scripts, which that heredoc already ran under). The gate imports them and lost its copies; the copy script's heredoc imports upstream_parts and its hand-written rpartition/partition split and its own DOCKER_HUB set are deleted. The gate's harness is unchanged at 99 assertions, which is what a refactor should leave; the tree mode passes with 12 rows and 35 references.
proof.negativeControl: The new case 'a library/golang row whose upstream names a host with a port' (registry.example.com:5000/library/golang:1.27.1-alpine, bytes carrying Go 1.26.3 against a tag naming 1.27.1) against the reviewed script: 'FAIL: fails', 'FAIL: names the reference it read and both versions', 'FAIL: and copies no golang row' — the old split read the host as part of the repository, so the row went past the check and into the package. All three pass at this head.

proof.criterion: Review round 4's three minor findings, and the job selection the new module needs
proof.surface: The repository's own gates over the real tree
proof.command: bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-action-pins.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-private-names.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-bun-version.sh ; bash .github/scripts/check-bun-version.test.sh
proof.observed: The refusal names the row's whole upstream (docker.io/library/golang:1.27.1-alpine, not golang:1.27.1, a different image) and which reference it read; the harness's dead fixtures, its dead 'upstream tag that has moved' case and the header prose the deleted upstream-tag read left behind are gone; the THE GO CHECK paragraph describes what the script does. .github/scripts/ci_images.py joined ci.yaml's ci_images filter and ci_job_reads.py's gate for that job, so a change to the module alone selects the ci-images job: check-ci-filters.sh passes with 25 gates and reports ci-images at 6 files, 0 uncovered. check-image-trigger-paths.sh passes with 5 image builds; every action is pinned; no private name; every Bun install reads .bun-version (1.4.4) with 119 assertions.
proof.negativeControl: check-ci-filters.sh is the control on the filter edit: it fails a job whose reads its filter misses, which is how the missing ci_images.py entry would have shown.

proof.criterion: The open risk of earlier rounds: merged-root-waits green on a hosted runner, which no settled run had shown
proof.surface: GitHub Actions, the E2E proofs workflow on a hosted runner
proof.command: gh workflow run e2e.yaml -R sjawhar/legion --ref legion/INFRA-567 -f script=merged-root-waits ; gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40999737194/jobs
proof.observed: Run 40999737194 at e719a7f2, which carries the restart fix of 35db766a: select success, merged-root-waits success. The earlier red at 368e3d2b was that restart defect, fixed before this run. This round changes only .github/scripts/ and ci.yaml's filter list, no daemon code, so it moves nothing that proof reads.
proof.negativeControl: The same proof at 368e3d2b, run 40979438094, failed at merged_root_waits_live_test.go:523 in step 5 with the five clone lines in daemon.log — the defect this change fixed.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/ci_images.py, new: the one reference reader, split_reference and upstream_parts with their grammar
.github/scripts/check-ci-images.sh and its harness: imports that module in place of its own copies, no behaviour change

.github/scripts/mirror-ci-images.sh and its harness: the package read first, the Go check on the package's copy for a held row and on the upstream before a copy, one parser, the refusal's wording, the header, and the dead fixtures removed
.github/workflows/ci.yaml and .github/scripts/ci_job_reads.py: ci_images.py as a file the ci-images job reads
openQuestions: The pod was re-pinned to a new worker image at 03:17Z, and that image carries no PyYAML, so every gate of this repository that reads a YAML file fails in it with ModuleNotFoundError. I installed pyyaml 6.0.3 into a user site on the issue volume (PYTHONUSERBASE) to run the checks; the hosted runners are unaffected. dispatch://INFRA-333 is the issue that carries that gap.

CI run 41003510761 is running at this code head, started by this round's code push. The runs at the three earlier code heads were each cancelled, by the 03:17Z drain or by this push's own concurrency group.
The gate's package half fails until this change's own ci-images job copies the per-digest tags, which is expected and is why this round ran the tree half alone.
discoveredComplexity: A copy that keeps the manifest digest makes the package's own copy and the upstream the same bytes, so a check that must read an image can read whichever of the two costs nothing: the package for a row it already holds, the upstream only where the run is going to read it anyway.
